precepts.text: Ye which have followed me, in the regeneration, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. So it ain't Michael and Gabriel and Uriel; it's talking about our own people.
precepts.point: Bishop: you know where you really see it stick out? When we on those quests, and we in the middle of the ocean, there ain't nothing else to do, and brothers don't be around. And then when you get off the ship, you see them coming back on the ship afterwards, like, nah, bro, you ain't with us. This is vacation.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” We are not judging Michael and Gabriel and them; that is not what it is talking about. Christ said: “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” It is talking about our own people. We shall judge the leaders.

“If then ye have judgments of things pertaining to this life, set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church.” The least esteemed are the young men, the lower ranked men. Raise those men up and use them. Stop wasting your time on brothers who have been around ten years and are doing nothing; they lack the zeal and the fire, and you have to force them to do everything, like a fizzle of wind.

Around the table you can see the ones with zeal: they have questions, they want to know, and when you read the scripture the fire is in them. Then there are the ones who stay in the back; you have to call them into the war room and they say, oh, I didn't know I could come in. That is a lie. In California, brother after brother gave the most outrageous answers because they do not study, and it is not just Cali. On the quests, in the middle of the ocean with nothing else to do, those brothers are not around; for them it is a vacation. That is a hireling.

The ones who will sit on thrones judging the tribes are the ones who follow Christ now, so give the work to the young men who want to learn and grow.

precepts.text: The Pharisees tempted him with Moses' writing of divorcement, Deuteronomy 24, and Christ took them back to the beginning: he which made them made them male and female, and they twain shall be one flesh; what God hath joined together, let not man put asunder. God did not join backdoor marriages. Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. Those are failsafe laws to keep negroes from going all the way wicked; you are not supposed to be in failure for them to come up, and quoting one after you went off does not make you righteous.
precepts.point: A sixth grader in the South stood up and put me on blast for a nasty note, and a sister in the world corrected an Israelite with a Bible in his hand, but grown women in the truth let men talk them out of their drawers and call it love.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
The Pharisees came to Christ “tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” They were trying to use Moses' law, the writing of divorcement in Deuteronomy 24. Christ took them back to the beginning: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?” From the beginning there was no such thing as divorce. What are you talking about, quoting Moses? It's the same as a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16.

“Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder”. God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That's why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call yourself love. You don't love anything but your own lust.

“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so”. The only reason Moses had to bring in that negro-proof law is that we were hard-headed and gave Moses hell. It is a failsafe law, a kind of bylaw to keep us from going all the way wicked. You are not supposed to be in failure at all for it even to come up, and quoting one after you went off and did wrong does not make you righteous.

That is covering violence with the garment: “for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the Lord of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously”. The Pharisees enlarged the borders of their garments, and the fringes represent the laws. A man who deceived to get a sister and then gives her a so-called law from the Bible is covering his violation with the law. Sisters and brothers, watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and stop playing games.

precepts.text: Ye shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: Set the young men with zeal to the work, and move the officers who always have an excuse.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?” The law they were going to was the scribes and Pharisees. Paul said, how dare you go to them? They do not even believe in Christ, and they do not apply the laws correctly. You are supposed to go to the saints.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” That is what Psalms 2 said: “be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” And the saints are not everybody who believes on Jesus: Psalms 148 says “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. The saints are the Israelites, and the Israelites will judge this planet. We might look like knuckles right now, but give us time.

“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we are going to judge are not Michael, Gabriel or Uriel; the angels are Israel, and we will judge each other. Christ said: “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

That is our future: judging the twelve tribes and the whole world. So how come we do not judge the small matters amongst ourselves? “set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church”. If the leaders act like they are unable to judge, get the young men; they can. Move the officers that always have an excuse out of the way, because the young men have the fire, the zeal, the desire and the understanding to do the job. “I speak to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?” All these years studying and not one wise brother that can handle this work? Then get the young ones.

precepts.text: What God hath joined together, let not man put asunder; Moses suffered divorce for the hardness of your hearts, but from the beginning it was not so.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
Christ magnified this law. The Pharisees came tempting him: “Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” He answered from the beginning: “he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.”

Then they asked the question that brings in the bill of divorcement: “Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away?” And he said, “Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.” The writing of divorcement given in her hand was suffered because of the hardness of hearts; it was not so from the beginning.

Then Christ set the bound on it: “Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.”

precepts.text: Some are born eunuchs and some are made eunuchs of men, as Daniel and his companions were made eunuchs after they were grown.
precepts.point: Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in Isaiah 39.

note.label: 2 Kings 20: Hezekiah's Healing and His Folly

precepts.why:
“For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men.”

Some are born eunuchs and some are made eunuchs of men. Daniel and his companions were made eunuchs of men, after they were grown, when they were carried to Babylon. So Isaiah’s word that Hezekiah’s sons “shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon” came to pass as it was spoken.

precepts.text: In the regeneration the Son of man sits in the throne of his glory and the servants judge the tribes of Israel, which is the day Job looks to.
precepts.point: Verses 25 through 27 are going into the regeneration; when you go back and read them, this is Job looking past the grave to seeing God for himself in a resurrected body.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

precepts.why:
“Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” In the regeneration the Son of man sits in the throne of his glory and the servants judge the tribes of Israel. That is the day Job looks to.

Verses 25 through 27 are going into the regeneration: “I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. When you go back and read them, this is Job looking past the grave to seeing God for himself in a resurrected body, “Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. That is why he wanted his words written, printed in a book, graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock forever, so that this testimony would stand.

precepts.text: Those who followed Christ in the regeneration shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Peter asked it plainly: “Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?” And Christ answered, “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” Those who followed Christ, in the regeneration, sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

So it is not true that there is no gain to a man in making his ways perfect. Eliphaz throws Job's righteousness back as filthy rags, asking “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?” But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. There is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

precepts.text: The bill of divorcement Moses allowed, given into her hand when he sent her out of his house.
precepts.point: The trouble in that day was men finding any cause at all to put a woman away. Whosoever putteth away his wife, except it be for fornication, and marrieth another, committeth adultery, and puts her into sin as well.

note.label: Matthew 19: Marriage, the Young Man's Possessions, and the Twelve Thrones

precepts.why:
“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away?” “Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.”

This is the bill of divorcement Moses allowed: “When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.” It was written for some uncleanness found in her, given into her hand when he sent her out of his house, and it was suffered because of the hardness of their hearts.

The trouble in that day was men finding any cause at all to put a woman away. Christ brings it back to the beginning: “Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.” The man who puts her away for anything but fornication and marries another commits adultery, and he puts her into sin as well, because whoever marries her commits adultery too.
